caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 325 of 2008 with Civil Rule No. 500(FM) of 2008.
lawyer:
Syed Mainul Haque with MG Mahmud (Shaheen) Advocates—For the Appellant. 
M Enayetur Rahim with Zahangir Alam, Advocates —For the Respondents.
parties:
Shahidul Islam Reza (Md) ----- Appellant
vs
Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Roumari, Kurigram and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the plaintiff-appellant this First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against the order dated 18-8-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Kurigram in Other Suit No. 09 of 2008 rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

 3. Sole plaintiff has filed Other Suit No. 9 of 2008 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Kurigram against the defendants-respondents for a declaration that the resolution dated 10-7-2008 passed by the governing body of the Jadur Char Model College suspending the appellant is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the appellant. 

 4. In that suit the appellant filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of temporary injunction so that his peaceful functioning as the Principal of the Jadur Char Model College has not been disturbed. In that application for temporary injunction the appellant contended that he was appointed as the principal of the aforesaid college on 1-4-99 and had been serving the college diligently to the satisfaction of others. Subsequently on 10-7-2008 a meeting of the governing body was held and in that so-called meeting the plaintiff was shown to be suspended. By letter dated 16-7-2008 issued by the defendant-respondent No. 1. The Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Roumari, who is the president of that college, the order of suspension dated 10-7-2008 was effected. Stating all these facts the appellant prayed for temporary injunction. The learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 24-7-2008 issued a show cause notice upon the defendant respondent Nos. 1 to 10 asking them why the order of temporary injunction should not be passed restraining them from disturbing the plaintiff-appellant in functioning as principal of the said college. The said application for temporary injunction was contested by the defendant-respondent Nos. 1 to 5 by filing written objection bringing some allegations, in particular, that the plaintiff-appellant misappropriated the money given by the defendant respondent No. 2 to deposit the same with bank as FDR. 

 6. Mr Syed Mainul Hoque appearing with Mr MG Mahmud, the learned Counsel after taking us through the impugned order appealed against has mainly argued that the governing body of the college acted without jurisdiction in suspending the plaintiff-appellants inasmuch as in so doing no inquiry was ever held and the suspension order is malafide which is not at all in keeping with the Recognised Non-government Intermediate College Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Rajshahi) Terms and Conditions of the Service Regulations, 1979. The learned Counsel after taking us through Annexure-A to the application for Temporary Injunction points out that without serving any show cause notice and without affording the appellant to defend him the order of suspension dated 10-7-2008 was passed which has clearly violated section 14 of the said Regulation, 1979. He submits that before makings an order of suspension it was incumbent upon the managing body of the college to issue a show cause notice upon the appellant giving 7 days' time so that he could give reply to such notice. Therefore, it is in clear violation of said regulation as mentioned above. The learned Counsel in support of his contention placed reliance in the decision of BN Khan College vs Md Abdul Rahim 7 BLT (AD) 153, (Bijoy Kumar Shaha vs DC, Chuadanga) 55 DLR 550. 

 "From the averments in the plaint, it is found that the suspension order was passed without prior show cause. The plaintiff having been adversely affected by the suspension order has filed the suit and, as such, it cannot be said that he has no cause of action to file the suit." 

 14. On the conspectus, we are of the view that under the facts and circumstances plaintiff-appellant had succeeded in proving that he had prima facie case that warranted an order of injunction by the trial Court and the trial Court without granting the relief has committed illegality. 

 16. Defendants are hereby restrained by an order of temporary injunction from disturbing the plaintiff-appellant in performing as principal of Jadur Char Model College till disposal of the suit.
